title: SmartShield Evaluation Corpus Expected Results Manifest

fixtures.manual_reasoning: Direct require(tx.origin == owner) authorization guard controlling ether transfer. If an owner interacts with a malicious contract, the attacker contract can invoke withdraw() and drain funds because tx.origin remains the legitimate owner.

Authorization predicate strictly compares msg.sender == owner. When an intermediary contract calls withdraw(), msg.sender evaluates to the calling contract rather than the owner, correctly reverting unauthorized access.

Authorization is decoupled from function bodies into an onlyOriginOwner modifier comparing tx.origin == owner. The modifier guards state mutation (transferOwnership) and ether drainage (emergencyWithdraw). Demonstrates modifier-based origin misuse.
fixtures.reference: ConsenSys Smart Contract Best Practices (Origin in Modifiers)

fixtures.manual_reasoning: Contains the tx.origin keyword for event logging (ActionLogged) and anti-bot verification (require(tx.origin == msg.sender)), but critical authorization is strictly guarded by require(msg.sender == owner). Demonstrates that keyword presence alone must not trigger a false positive.

Vulnerable authorization check tx.origin == owner is delegated through an internal library call (OriginAuthLib.isOriginOwner). Because Sprint 1 intra-contract CFG and Call Graph do not resolve inter-library delegatecall state, this is tracked explicitly as an analysis limitation rather than a false negative.

Classic single-function reentrancy. The low-level external call payable(msg.sender).call{value: amount}("") is executed before balances[msg.sender] is decremented. A malicious recipient fallback can reenter withdraw() and drain the vault before the state mutation executes.

Complies strictly with the Checks-Effects-Interactions pattern. The user balance balances[msg.sender] -= amount is decremented prior to the low-level value transfer, preventing reentrant double-spend attacks.

Cross-function reentrancy vulnerability. withdrawAll() executes an external call before setting userBalances[msg.sender] = 0. The recipient reenters via transferTo(recipient, amount), which reads the unzeroed balance to double-spend funds to an accomplice account.

Even though state mutation balances[msg.sender] -= amount occurs after the low-level call, the function is protected by an explicit nonReentrant mutex lock. Reentrant callbacks revert during the modifier check.

Read-only reentrancy where removeLiquidity sends an external callback while totalShares and reserves are temporarily inconsistent. getPricePerShare() is a view function with no post-call state write, making single-contract intra-procedural CFG unable to detect it without cross-contract oracle modeling.
fixtures.reference: Curve LP / Sentiment Read-Only Reentrancy Exploits (2023)
